style: Hand-drawn 2D cartoon illustration for a YouTube history explainer. Simple stick-figure people with large round plain white heads, black dot eyes, expressive eyebrows, small simple mouths, messy dark hair, thin black stick arms and legs, teal striped hide tunics with a tooth necklace; thick clean black ink outlines, flat bright colors with soft painterly shading, richly detailed painted cartoon backgrounds (caves, savanna, firelight, starry skies). Funny, gentle, not gory. 16:9 widescreen. Absolutely no text, letters, captions or watermark in the image.

shots.p: Lush misty rainforest at dawn in Borneo with a limestone cliff and cave mouth; a small stick-figure child sits on a leaf mat by a fire wearing a neat leaf bandage on the lower left leg, while a kind adult hands them a wooden bowl, everyone calm and gentle.
shots.line: Thirty-one thousand years ago, in a rainforest in Borneo, a child had part of their leg removed by surgery.

shots.p: The same rainforest child, a few years older, grinning and walking with a wooden crutch beside friends along a jungle path, birds and big leaves around, warm sunlight.
shots.line: And the child survived. For years.

shots.p: Three-panel gag: a hospital sign crossed out by a giant painted X, a metal scalpel crossed out, and a tiny cartoon germ wearing a disguise and a fake moustache, against a painted cave wall.
shots.line: No hospitals. No metal tools. No idea that germs even existed.

shots.p: Hero shot: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sitting by a cave fire wrapped in a hide blanket, nose red, eyebrows worried, holding his tummy, a painted sunset valley behind.
shots.line: So what did ancient humans actually do when they got sick?

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) as a tiny figure under three giant floating question marks made of twisted vines, a herb, a stone knife and a pair of helping hands drifting around him.
shots.line: Did they have medicine? Did they have doctors? Did anybody look after them?

shots.p: A warm circle of stick-figure cave people gently tucking a hide blanket around a sick friend by the fire, one bringing a bowl of soup, golden firelight glow.
shots.line: The answer is cleverer, and kinder, than you might think.

shots.p: Close-up of Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) lying dramatically on a grass bed, back of his hand on his forehead, a small cut on his arm, a crow on a rock looking unimpressed.
shots.line: Meet Moss. He has a sore tummy, a cut on his arm,

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sighing theatrically as a tiny violin-playing cricket sits on a stone beside him; cosy cave interior, funny tone.
shots.line: and a very bad case of feeling sorry for himself.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) peeking through big jungle leaves at a family of chimpanzees in a forest clearing, eyebrows raised with curiosity.
shots.line: To see where medicine might have started, let's first visit our cousins.

shots.p: Lush green slopes of the Mahale Mountains beside a shining blue lake in Tanzania; a lone tired-looking female chimpanzee sitting slumped at the foot of a leafy shrub, a tiny human observer with a notebook hiding behind a tree in the distance.
shots.line: In 1987, in the Mahale Mountains of Tanzania, scientists watched a sick chimpanzee do something odd.

shots.p: Close-up of the chimpanzee carefully peeling the outer bark from a shrub stem and chewing the pale pith inside, with a scrunched-up 'this tastes bad' face.
shots.line: She peeled the bark off a shrub, and slowly chewed the bitter pith inside.

shots.p: The chimpanzee pulling a hilariously disgusted face with its tongue out, little stink lines rising from the green stem, other chimps watching from a branch.
shots.line: Chimps hardly ever eat that plant. It tastes horrible.

shots.p: A friendly village healer in a sunlit East African village holding up a sprig of the same bitter-leaf shrub, the shrub growing by a hut, gentle and respectful.
shots.line: But local people use the very same plant for tummy troubles and worms.

shots.p: The chimpanzee next morning, perky and bright-eyed, climbing a tree with energy, sunrise glow and birds.
shots.line: Within about a day, the chimp seemed to be feeling better.

shots.p: Science-lab style cartoon: a magnifying glass over the plant pith revealing tiny cartoon worms fleeing in panic from green sparkles.
shots.line: Later tests found the plant contains chemicals that work against some of the worms chimps carry.

shots.p: Dense Sumatran rainforest canopy; a big orange male orangutan with wide cheek pads sitting on a branch with a small scratch on his right cheek, looking grumpy.
shots.line: Then, in 2022, in Sumatra, an orangutan called Rakus hurt his face, probably in a fight.

shots.p: The orangutan chewing a bundle of leaves from a climbing vine with yellow stems and carefully dabbing the green juice onto his cheek with his fingers, focused expression.
shots.line: So he chewed up a climbing plant, and smeared the juice right onto the wound.

shots.p: Close-up of the orangutan pressing a neat pad of chewed green plant onto his cheek like a sticking plaster, looking quietly proud.
shots.line: Then he pressed the chewed plant on top. Like a little green plaster.

shots.p: The yellow-stemmed climbing vine winding up a rainforest tree, with soft glowing sparkles around its leaves, a few tiny cartoon germs running away.
shots.line: That plant is used in local medicine to fight swelling and germs.

shots.p: A calendar of five big leaves turning one by one, ending with the orangutan smiling with a fully healed cheek, sunlight through the canopy.
shots.line: Five days later, the wound had closed, with no sign of infection.

shots.p: The orangutan posing proudly like a doctor with a leaf clipboard, a small star-shaped badge on a vine around his neck, jungle background.
shots.line: Scientists think it's the first time a wild animal has been seen treating a wound with a medicinal plant.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) and an orangutan sitting side by side on a log, each holding a leaf and comparing notes, mirrored curious faces.
shots.line: So if apes can do it, our ancestors probably could too.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) tasting a leaf, making a face, then smiling as his tummy feels better, and drawing the leaf on a cave wall for children who watch closely; shown as one wide scene with the stages left to right.
shots.line: Scientists think early medicine may have grown from the same instinct: try a plant, feel better, remember it, pass it on.

shots.p: A friendly Neanderthal with a big nose and brow ridge sitting in a Spanish cave chewing a poplar twig, one cheek puffed up, holding his jaw, poplar trees outside.
shots.line: Remember the Neanderthal from our teeth video, who may have chewed poplar, a natural source of painkiller?

shots.p: A cave wall with a chain of painted handprints connecting a chimp, an orangutan and a Neanderthal, linked by a vine of medicinal leaves.
shots.line: That fits the pattern.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) putting down a basket of herbs and looking towards a group of friends by the fire, thoughtful expression.
shots.line: But medicine isn't only about plants.

shots.p: A group of cave people forming a warm huddle and offering their hands to someone, the hands glowing softly like medicine in the firelight.
shots.line: Sometimes, the medicine is people.

shots.p: Huge cave mouth of Shanidar Cave in the rugged Zagros mountains of Iraq, a burly friendly Neanderthal man standing in the entrance, golden evening light.
shots.line: About fifty thousand years ago, in Shanidar Cave in Iraq, there lived a Neanderthal man.

shots.p: The young Neanderthal man sitting dazed beside a fallen rock in a cave, a gentle bump and a star circling his head, friends rushing over (no blood).
shots.line: Early in life, he took a terrible blow to the head.

shots.p: The older Neanderthal man with a patch over one eye, his right arm ending at the elbow and wrapped in hide, smiling bravely by the fire.
shots.line: He was probably blind in one eye. One arm was withered, and later lost at the elbow.

shots.p: The Neanderthal man walking with a stick and a slight limp, cupping his ear as a friend shouts cheerfully into it, small sound-wave lines.
shots.line: He walked with a limp. And scientists think he was very hard of hearing.

shots.p: Cartoon X-ray style view of the Neanderthal's bones with soft golden glows over old healed places, the man giving a thumbs up.
shots.line: But all of those injuries had healed.

shots.p: The Neanderthal man, now grey-haired and wrinkled, sitting proudly on a rock with a birthday-like ring of forty little pebbles around him, the group smiling.
shots.line: And he lived to around forty, or even older. That's old for a Neanderthal.

shots.p: The Neanderthal man looking puzzled at a spear while, in the distance, a lion's ears poke above tall grass behind him; comic tension.
shots.line: How do you hunt like that? Or hear a lion coming?

shots.p: Two young Neanderthals bringing the older man a share of meat and walking beside him, one pointing out the distant lion, all safe and cosy.
shots.line: Scientists think the answer is simple. Other people helped him.

shots.p: A scientist in a modern lab examining a tiny ear bone under a big glowing magnifier, a framed drawing of a small Neanderthal girl on the wall, a cave in Spain shown in a window.
shots.line: In a cave in Spain, scientists studied a tiny ear bone from a Neanderthal child they nicknamed Tina.

shots.p: A small smiling Neanderthal girl with a tuft of hair, sitting close to her mother, little swirly dizzy spirals above her head, warm cave interior.
shots.line: Its shape suggests Tina may have had Down syndrome, with poor hearing and bad dizzy spells.

shots.p: The Neanderthal girl, now six, holding up six fingers proudly beside a ring of cheering family in a sunny Mediterranean valley.
shots.line: Yet Tina lived to at least six years old.

shots.p: Several Neanderthal adults sharing the care of the little girl: one carrying her on their back, one feeding her berries, one holding her hand on a walk.
shots.line: Scientists think her mother couldn't have managed alone. The whole group probably pitched in.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) grinning by the fire with his arm around two friends who bring him soup and a fresh hide blanket.
shots.line: So long before there were doctors, there were friends.

shots.p: A circle of hands of all sizes holding a small glowing heart-shaped stone over a sleeping figure, soft starry night above the cave.
shots.line: Being looked after may be one of the oldest medicines of all.

shots.p: A journey-map style painting zooming back across the sea to the green mountainous island of Borneo, a cave marked by a glowing dot.
shots.line: Which brings us back to Borneo.

shots.p: Archaeologists in hats gently brushing soil in a limestone cave in Borneo, a carefully laid-out skeleton half-revealed, a sieve and a notebook nearby, calm and respectful.
shots.line: In 2020, scientists digging in a cave called Liang Tebo found a skeleton.

shots.p: A respectful cartoon skeleton lying on its back with knees bent in a neat grave, two archaeologists kneeling beside it.
shots.line: It belonged to a young person, about nineteen or twenty years old.

shots.p: Close-up diagram-style painting of the skeleton's legs: the left lower leg simply ends a little above the ankle, a soft glowing outline showing where the missing part would be.
shots.line: And the lower part of their left leg was missing.

shots.p: Cartoon diagram of a neat, smooth, rounded healed leg-bone end next to a jagged broken twig for comparison, a magnifier hovering above.
shots.line: The bone ended neatly, and it had healed over smoothly.

shots.p: A side-by-side comparison card: a cartoon crocodile and a falling rock both crossed out, a careful stone blade and a leaf bandage ticked; rainforest background.
shots.line: Scientists think this wasn't an accident, or an animal attack. It was a planned operation.

shots.p: Gentle cave scene: a calm child lying on a leaf bed while a caring adult prepares leaves and a bowl, others holding the child's hand; no wounds shown, soft firelight.
shots.line: From the way the bone grew, the surgery probably happened when they were a child.

shots.p: The young person growing up through a sequence of seasons in the rainforest: child, teen, young adult, always with a crutch and smiling friends nearby.
shots.line: They then lived for another six to nine years.

shots.p: Tiny cartoon germs knocking at a leaf-curtained cave door while a caring adult holds up glowing green rainforest leaves to keep them out.
shots.line: So how did they avoid a deadly infection?

shots.p: Rainforest healer grinding colourful leaves and roots in a stone bowl, steam curling up, lush Borneo jungle and limestone peaks behind.
shots.line: Nobody knows for sure. But the scientists suggest rainforest plants with medicinal powers may have helped.

shots.p: Steep jagged limestone karst hills covered in jungle, a tiny figure with a crutch at the bottom of a steep path looking up.
shots.line: And this person lived in steep, rocky, jungle hills.

shots.p: Two friends helping the young person with a crutch up a rocky jungle slope, one carrying their basket, one offering an arm, cheerful and determined.
shots.line: Getting around on one leg there would have needed a lot of help, for a lot of years.

shots.p: A peaceful cave at dusk with a neat grave marked by a few limestone stones, a sprig of leaves laid on top, friends standing quietly with bowed heads.
shots.line: When they died, they were buried with care, with stones placed over the grave.

shots.p: A cartoon timeline stretching across a cave wall: a small marker labelled with a Neolithic farmer figure in France near the right end, and a far older marker with the Borneo cave far to the left.
shots.line: Before this, the oldest known amputation was about seven thousand years old, from France.

shots.p: The Borneo marker sliding far back along the timeline with speed lines, the farmer figure's jaw dropping in surprise.
shots.line: Borneo pushed that back by twenty-four thousand years.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) with eyebrows shooting up in alarm, his hands flying to protect his head, firelit cave background, comic timing.
shots.line: But there's an even stranger kind of Stone Age surgery.

shots.p: A stone-age skull drawn like a friendly museum specimen on a cushion, a soft spotlight on it, curious onlookers peering in.
shots.line: And it involves the head.

shots.p: A calm museum-style cartoon of a skull with a small neat round opening on top, a tidy flint scraper and a bowl of herbs laid beside it on a hide cloth; no blood, no patient visible.
shots.line: It's called trepanation. Making a small hole in a living person's skull,

shots.p: Close-up of a careful hand holding a small flint scraper beside a bowl of herbs, a patient's peaceful sleeping face in soft focus, wrapped in a warm hide; gentle, no wound visible.
shots.line: by slowly scraping or cutting through the bone with stone tools.

shots.p: An archaeological dig in green farmland in Alsace, France with a church tower far off; archaeologists gently uncover a burial of a man with a skull showing two small round marks.
shots.line: At Ensisheim, in France, archaeologists found a man buried around seven thousand years ago.

shots.p: Close-up of the skull with two neat round openings, each circled by a friendly glowing yellow ring, two pebbles placed beside it.
shots.line: His skull had not one, but two of these holes.

shots.p: Diagram-style close-up of one opening with soft new bone growing back around the rim like a healing moss, and the other opening fully filled in.
shots.line: And around the edges, new bone had grown back. One hole had closed over completely.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) holding up two fingers, cheering, as a heart-rate-style line of green leaves bounces happily across the cave wall behind him.
shots.line: Bone only heals in someone who's alive. So he survived. Twice.

shots.p: A world map painted on a large hide with little glowing skull markers in Europe, South America, Africa and Asia.
shots.line: He's not alone. Healed trepanned skulls turn up in many parts of the ancient world.

shots.p: A line of cheerful ancient people from different places, each with a small neat bandage around their head, waving.
shots.line: Many patients lived on afterwards.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) scratching his head in confusion, three thought bubbles above him showing a bump on the head, a headache cloud, and a small cartoon spirit.
shots.line: Why do it? Nobody is completely sure.

shots.p: A friendly cartoon spirit with puffed cheeks being gently let out of a jar into the sky, symbolising an old belief, soft colourful painterly sky.
shots.line: Maybe to treat a head injury, or bad headaches, or something people believed was trapped inside.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) wagging his finger at the viewer with a stern-but-funny expression, standing in front of a pile of stone tools.
shots.line: Either way, please don't try this at home.

shots.p: A snowy high Alpine pass with jagged peaks; a man in a grass cloak and fur hat carrying a backpack frame, a leather pouch and strings of fungus at his belt.
shots.line: Now let's meet a patient who carried his own first-aid kit.

shots.p: Two cartoon hikers in 1990s outdoor gear on a glacier, pointing in surprise at a figure frozen in a block of blue ice, bright Alpine sky.
shots.line: In 1991, hikers in the Alps found a man frozen in the ice. He'd died about five thousand three hundred years ago.

shots.p: Portrait of the Iceman Otzi as a friendly stick figure with a beard, fur cap and grass cape, standing in front of a modern museum glass case.
shots.line: Scientists call him Otzi, the Iceman.

shots.p: Close-up of two lumps of brown birch polypore fungus threaded onto leather strips, laid on fur beside a copper axe and a quiver, soft museum lighting.
shots.line: And among his belongings were lumps of a fungus, threaded onto leather strips.

shots.p: A white bracket fungus growing on a birch tree trunk in a forest, tiny cartoon germs running away from it in fright.
shots.line: It's called birch polypore, and it contains natural chemicals that fight germs.

shots.p: Cartoon cross-section of a tummy with tiny wiggly cartoon worms looking cheeky, and the Iceman wincing and holding his belly in the snow.
shots.line: Inside Otzi's gut, scientists found the eggs of whipworm, a parasite that can cause tummy pain.

shots.p: The Iceman nibbling a small piece of the fungus with a hopeful expression, a cartoon worm waving a white flag.
shots.line: So some scientists think the fungus may have been his medicine.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) and the Iceman shrugging together beside a big painted question mark carved into the ice.
shots.line: We can't know for sure. But it would make sense.

shots.p: The Iceman's bare back and legs shown in a calm, friendly diagram, decorated with small dark parallel lines and little crosses as tattoos.
shots.line: Otzi also had sixty-one tattoos. Not pictures, just little lines and crosses.

shots.p: Diagram of the Iceman with soft red glows over his lower back, knees and ankles, the tattoo lines sitting right on top of them, him rubbing his knee.
shots.line: Many sit over his lower back, knees and ankles, places where his joints were worn and may well have ached.

shots.p: Two cartoon scientists in front of a chart of the Iceman's tattoo spots, one nodding with a leaf pointer, one with arms crossed and a sceptical eyebrow.
shots.line: Some scientists think the tattoos may have been a kind of pain treatment.

shots.p: Split scene: two scientists playfully tugging on opposite ends of a long vine labelled with tattoo lines, an amused Iceman watching.
shots.line: Others aren't convinced. The debate is still going.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) sitting cosily by the cave fire, wrapped in a blanket, starting to smile, as friends arrive with baskets.
shots.line: So, here's what getting sick might have looked like for Moss.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) chewing a bitter leaf with a scrunched face while a friend dabs green plant paste onto the small cut on his arm.
shots.line: A bitter plant for his sore tummy. A green plant paste on his cut.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) tucked up by the fire as friends bring him a bowl of food and add another hide blanket, warm golden firelight.
shots.line: And if things got really bad, friends who brought him food, and kept him warm.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) looking thoughtful by the fire with an honest, slightly sad expression, a little magic wand lying unused in the dirt.
shots.line: Of course, ancient medicine wasn't magic.

shots.p: A quiet painted night landscape with a camp under the stars, a few gentle shooting stars, a soft respectful mood.
shots.line: Lots of people still died from things we can treat easily today.

shots.p: Return to the Borneo rainforest cave at dawn: the young person with a crutch standing tall at the cave mouth, friends around them, sunrise lighting the jungle.
shots.line: But remember that child in Borneo, thirty-one thousand years ago?

shots.p: A careful adult laying out leaves and a stone tool on a hide with a determined, gentle face, then a group carrying a basket of food to the young person, shown as one warm scene.
shots.line: Someone made a brave, careful plan to save them. And then people looked after them, for years.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) holding a leaf up to the light and then dropping it with a knowing smile, friends gathering around him.
shots.line: Maybe the oldest medicine wasn't a plant at all.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) and a whole group of cave people walking together across a sunset hillside, the strongest helping the slowest, all holding hands.
shots.line: Maybe it was people refusing to leave anyone behind.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) waving goodbye at the cave mouth, healthy and happy with a small leaf plaster on his arm, friends waving behind him, warm sunset.
shots.line: Follow for more of how ancient humans really lived.
